$comment: templates/workflow.json -- the default `nen/workflow.json` document `nen scaffold init` and `nen scaffold new` write into absence, and the ONE place those bytes are written down. It is DATA for the same reason every other file under templates/ is: src/scaffold/ carries no name it did not have to, and a reviewer can read every byte nen would write into somebody's repository without reading a line of TypeScript. src/scaffold/templates.ts's `defaultWorkflowDocument()` is the only reader; it overlays exactly three values the CALLER states -- `iteration.lane` (the lane being scaffolded), `commits.allowedAttributionTrailers` (the one trailer key --agent-trailer resolved to -- its own default, Akatsuki-Agent, or a caller override) and `commits.runTrailer` (the key --run-trailer named, or null) -- and copies the rest verbatim.
$defaults: Every value under `document` except `models` restates the default src/schema/workflow.ts applies when the file is ABSENT, and src/scaffold/workflow-default.test.ts pins that agreement in both directions so the two cannot drift. `models` is the exception on purpose: nen has no default for it, because a default there would be nen inventing a name. The pack states a starting matrix a maintainer edits or deletes; the loader, reading a file that omits the block, answers with an empty one.
$defaultAgentTrailerComment: src/scaffold/command.ts's `--agent-trailer` falls back to this key when a caller states none (zheref/nen#167) -- this project family's own CI-plane provenance trailer, ratified by the maintainer's 2026-09-10 ruling (zheref/nen#164, docs/USAGE.md's 'Two provenance trailers'). It is DATA, read here by src/scaffold/templates.ts's `defaultAgentTrailer()`, rather than a literal in shipped TypeScript: src/taxonomy-purity.test.ts's §3 sweep forbids a hard-coded system/persona name in executable code, and a caller who wants a different key still overrides it with --agent-trailer <key>.

document.$comment: Written by `nen scaffold init`. This file is POLICY -- what the delivery loop's parameters are. What nen EXECUTES lives in nen/contract.json. Every key here is optional and carries the default nen applies when it is absent; delete anything you do not want to state. `nen schema check` validates it.

notifications.$comment: turn decides how loud an ORDINARY (no-gate) turn is: 'rung1' rings only the first rung 'rungs' lists, 'all' rings every rung 'rungs' lists on every turn -- a gate always rings everything 'rungs' lists regardless.

commits.$comment: Hatsu-Agent (a local-plane agent, working on a human's own credentials) and Akatsuki-Agent (an autonomous CI-plane agent) are the two conventional provenance-trailer keys this project's family uses -- never an AI-authorship claim. nen ships neither as a default: this list stays empty until a repository states which of the two (or both) it admits, e.g. ["Hatsu-Agent", "Akatsuki-Agent"]. `nen scaffold init`'s own --agent-trailer defaults to Akatsuki-Agent and writes its resolved key here for you. runTrailer is a SEPARATE, OPTIONAL key, e.g. "Akatsuki-Run" -- absent (null) by default, and never itself an attribution trailer: it names which RUN produced a commit, not who or what did, so it never belongs in the list above. Set it (--run-trailer, then re-run 'nen scaffold init' to regenerate the hook) only if this repository also wants a run identifier required on every automated commit.

models.$comment: An open map at both levels: a surface is whatever you call it, a tier likewise. nen validates that every leaf is a string and reads nothing else -- these aliases are for whoever asks the question, not for nen.
models.rule: latest alias only, never a version; subagents never on the frontier tier

cursor.note: surface-native aliases only; provider models on this surface are reserved for its own review bot
